scope: Exactly three unchanged committed tools are packaged with a JSON manifest. This prepares a first read-only inventory without cloning or installing the foundation branch. No SSH, ROS graph access, motor commands, Pi execution, policy execution, installer or restore action occurred.

archive.payload: Three reviewed tools under foundation/scripts, manifest.json, and containing directories only. Local smoke outputs and evidence are excluded from the transfer archive.
archive.file_mode: 0600; invoke the shell script using bash
archive.historical_manifest_note: The unchanged archive manifest was created before the Linux smoke and retains its original macOS-only runtime note. This separate hashed Linux addendum expands validation without altering the transfer bytes.

dependencies.base: Bash and Python >=3.8 standard-library/POSIX file APIs. Actual base-path smokes passed on macOS arm64 Python 3.15.2 and isolated Linux aarch64 Python 3.12.3; no third-party Python package is imported by the base inventory.
dependencies.absent_optional_tools: Recorded as unavailable; base inventory does not require them. Python package versions are queried through importlib.metadata without importing those packages.

local_validation.description_helper: Library only; imported and exercised by non-ROS inventory and existing tests. No standalone CLI or --help interface.

usage.component_paths: Use --monorepo-dir, --gemini-dir, --follower-dir and --deployment-dir with independently discovered real paths when components live separately. Unspecified candidates are labeled unverified; a checkout path is not proof of active installation.
usage.ros: Do not add --ros until the existing approved ROS environment is known and read-only graph sampling is intentionally requested. The kit does not install ROS or launch anything.

limitations: Tested on macOS and an isolated Linux aarch64 container, not Pupper. Pi runtime, installed paths, active launch and ROS environment still require the first real inventory.
Python 3.8 syntax and standard-library API dependencies were inspected; actual runtimes tested were Python 3.15.2 and 3.12.3. This does not establish every interpreter/OS combination.
Package-version metadata and explicit local file hashes do not prove the active robot installation. The tool retains unverified path labels.
An inventory output contains local paths and software/runtime metadata and should remain private. No camera frames or credential values are deliberately captured.
The backup helper is bundled because inventory uses fingerprint_file; its separate explicit-copy CLI is not an installer or restore and was not invoked for backup creation here.

linux_validation.scope: Additive isolated Linux portability receipt; no Pi validation, installation, ROS graph use or hardware actions. The transfer archive and original manifest remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
linux_validation.git_metadata_limit: The read-only source mount contains a Git worktree pointer to host metadata outside the mount. Git is present but reports returncode128 for commit/branch/status; these structured failures remain in the inventory. No extra mount or clone was added. File hashing and description inspection still succeed.
linux_validation.initial_harness_failure: Attempt v1 completed help, bundled-module imports and inventory JSON/path/read-only assertions, then failed an invalid auxiliary assumption that /sys/class/net contains only lo. Linuxkit exposes default tunnel pseudo-interfaces and bonding_masters. Attempt v2 records these honestly and verifies the actual Docker NetworkMode=none, no passed devices, read-only mounts and an empty IPv4 route table. No network request or connection was attempted. The original failed stdout/stderr/receipt/script are preserved.
